subject: surgery
title: Congenital Anomalies of the Urinary Tract

steps.tx: Fusion of the lower poles of the two kidneys across the midline forms a **horseshoe kidney**. The joined isthmus lies in front of the great vessels and stops the kidneys rising to their normal level. Most people never know they have one unless a scan is done.
steps.say: A horseshoe kidney joins both lower poles across the midline, and most people only discover it on a scan.

steps.tx: Lower poles of the two kidneys fuse across the midline, forming a **horseshoe kidney** whose isthmus crosses near the third lumbar vertebra. On a coronal CT or an intravenous urogram the bridge sits anterior to the aorta and inferior vena cava, and that position blocks ascent to the usual renal height. Many people remain unaware of the anomaly until imaging is performed for another reason. The outline resembles a horseshoe opening upward.
steps.say: Lower poles of the two kidneys fuse across the midline, forming a horseshoe kidney whose isthmus crosses near the third lumbar vertebra. On a coronal CT or an intravenous urogram the bridge sits anterior to the aorta and inferior vena cava, and that position blocks ascent to the usual renal height. Many people remain unaware of the anomaly until imaging is performed for another reason. The outline resembles a horseshoe opening upward.

vis.alt: Coronal view of both kidneys with lower poles joined by an isthmus across the midline near L3
vis.caption: Both lower poles join in an isthmus crossing near L3, anterior to the aorta and inferior vena cava. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Complete failure of one kidney to develop is called **renal agenesis**. The opposite kidney grows larger to compensate and usually gives normal function. Bilateral agenesis is incompatible with life because no urine fills the amniotic sac. Bilateral agenesis causes Potter syndrome, with flattened facies and underdeveloped lungs because amniotic fluid is mostly fetal urine.
steps.say: Renal agenesis leaves one kidney absent, and the other grows larger to keep overall function normal.

steps.tx: A kidney lying outside its normal loin position is an **ectopic kidney**. It most often sits in the pelvis and may be found during pelvic examination or scanning. Ectopic kidneys drain poorly and are prone to stones and infection. A pelvic kidney is often mistaken for a pelvic tumour, and its blood supply is variable, so surgery on it needs careful planning.
steps.say: An ectopic kidney sits in the pelvis instead of the loin and is prone to stones and infection.

steps.tx: Two separate collecting systems draining one kidney form a **duplex system**. The upper part often drains into an abnormal low opening while the lower part tends to reflux. Many duplex systems cause no trouble and need no treatment. The Weigert-Meyer rule states the upper part ureter opens lower and medially, while the lower part ureter opens higher and tends to reflux.
steps.say: A duplex system gives one kidney two drainage systems, though many cause no trouble at all.

steps.tx: A balloon like swelling of the lower ureter inside the bladder is a **ureterocele**. It can block urine flow and cause infection, especially in children with duplex systems. Small ones may only need observation while obstructing ones need endoscopic opening. In girls a ureterocele can prolapse and appear as a small mass at the urethral opening, a rare but classic presentation.
steps.say: A ureterocele balloons inside the bladder and can block urine flow, especially in children with duplex systems.

steps.tx: The junction where renal pelvis funnels into ureter is a narrow doorway, and in this condition it never fully opens. **Pelviureteric junction obstruction** backs urine into a ballooning pelvis, stretching calyces while the ureter below stays slim, the pattern intravenous urography and renography map before surgery. Congenital muscle disorganisation causes most cases, crossing vessels the rest. Watching the split function on serial scans decides between pyeloplasty and patience, since many mild cases drain adequately despite their dramatic pictures.
steps.say: Pelviureteric junction obstruction dilates the renal pelvis above a narrow junction, threatening function if drainage fails.

vis.caption: Pelviureteric junction obstruction. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Narrowing where the renal pelvis joins the ureter is **pelviureteric junction obstruction**. It causes loin pain after drinking large volumes and slowly stretches the kidney. Untreated obstruction gradually destroys kidney tissue. The Dietl crisis describes severe loin pain with a palpable swollen kidney after a large drink, settling as urine flow resumes.
steps.say: Pelviureteric junction obstruction narrows the kidney outlet, causing loin pain after drinks and slow kidney damage.

steps.tx: The standard operation that removes the narrowed segment and rejoins the ureter widely is the **Anderson-Hynes pyeloplasty**. It creates a funnel shaped, dependent drainage path for urine. Success rates are high in both children and adults. Success rates exceed 90 percent, and a temporary stent is often left for a few weeks while the new join heals.
steps.say: Anderson-Hynes pyeloplasty removes the narrowed segment and rebuilds a wide funnel for urine drainage.

steps.tx: A nuclear medicine scan that tracks tracer washout from the kidney is the **DTPA renogram**. Poor washout that improves after a water pill suggests a drainage problem rather than a dead kidney. It also tells how much each kidney contributes. Split function below about 10 percent suggests that kidney contributes little, which changes whether repair is worthwhile at all.
steps.say: A DTPA renogram tracks tracer washout and shows both drainage and each kidney share of function.

steps.tx: A ureter passing behind the inferior vena cava is a **retrocaval ureter**. The vein compresses it and causes right sided kidney swelling. Surgery divides and rejoins the ureter in front of the vein to restore drainage. It is almost always right sided, because only the right ureter can be trapped behind the inferior vena cava.
steps.say: A retrocaval ureter passes behind the great vein, gets compressed, and needs surgical rejoining in front.

steps.tx: Gross underdevelopment of the bladder with exposed mucosa at birth is **bladder exstrophy**. It occurs with epispadias, where the urethra opens on the upper surface of the penis. Early surgical closure and later reconstruction aim to protect kidneys and continence. The exposed bladder plate is closed in the first days of life, and pelvic bone cuts may be needed to close it without tension.
steps.say: Bladder exstrophy exposes the bladder at birth with epispadias, and staged surgery protects kidneys and continence.
